title: converting a Result to a string yields its own type tag rather than a bare object tag
notes: A DELIBERATE PIN OF AN UNSPECIFIED DIFFERENCE, written so it is found on purpose rather than discovered as a mystery inside some later case. conformance/README.md, 'How an output case is observed', records that the two backends represent a Result differently at run time and that the harness duck-types both into the same printed lines — 'Normalizing the representation is what makes one declared expectation legitimately comparable across two implementations.' A program that stringifies a Result reaches AROUND that normalization and observes the representation directly, so ANY corpus case that does so will diverge until this is settled. The reference runtime declares `get [Symbol.toStringTag]() { return "Result" }`; the fork's emitted prelude classes declare none, so the same program prints `[object Object]` there. NO SPECIFICATION SENTENCE COVERS THIS, which the marker states plainly. The second line is here on purpose: it proves the Result is still an ordinary must-use value that is consumed by unwrapping it, so the case cannot be satisfied by a backend that made `String(found)` itself a consumption. THE `xfail(go)` MARKER WAS RETIRED 2026-08-28: both of the fork's prelude classes now declare `get [Symbol.toStringTag]() { return "Result" }`, so both backends print `[object Result]`. The marker's stated blocker was not that the fix was hard but that it would move the emitted bytes of every Go-compiled program and spoil a byte-for-byte emit comparison; the same commit that closes this row already moved those bytes by teaching the fork's prelude `flatten` and `tapBoth`, so the objection had already been spent and the one-line fix was taken in the same pass rather than left as an unexplained diff in a later case. THE DIFFERENCE REMAINS UNSPECIFIED — specification/* still says nothing about a Result's runtime string tag, and this case, not a spec sentence, is what now holds the two backends to the same answer. conformance/README.md is what makes it corpus-relevant: the harness normalizes the two runtime representations for every OTHER observation, so this is the one channel through which the difference is visible to a case at all.
